items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: We came to New York with Mamie Smith. She came down -- she was married to a Jewish fella by the name of Bert Goldberg and they came down and got us and we played some theaters and Tim and Freddie -- Timmie Rogers and Freddie was together. We played theaters with her.

ctx.x: Had you been aware of Hawkins before?

Yeah. Yeah, I knew he was with Fletcher and I had listened to him, but I wasn't really -- he wasn't my idol -- Prince is like -- as much as Prince was, you know, until, of course, after that, I loved him, you know, I really did love him. And then everybody was like -- he gained the recognition as being the world's greatest saxophone player, you know, tenor player, because he really did really introduce the instrument. There's no stuff about that, you know, like even when Mamie Smith, when he was playing with…
Why do you think that was?

items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: I worked with Mamie, in later years.

ctx.x: They were singing the Blues, like Mamie Smith, Bessie Smith, Ma Rainey and all of them you know, and they were trying to get away from it. Like what was that other one [sings] If you had plenty money, like 1922, you wouldn’t be here, why don’t you do right like the other folk do, go out and give me some money too. That was made by Ma Rainey, and she was older than Mamie Smith. I worked with Mamie, in later years. And she was older than Mamie Smith. And they didn’t make no money on that. Many did, and Peggy did,…
Any other little anecdotes you’d like to give us?
